translator: Thomas Common (poetry rendered by Paul V. Cohn and Maude D. Petre)
method: Downloaded Gutenberg UTF-8 plain text (52124-0.txt), sliced from Nietzsche's Preface to the Second Edition through the end of the closing poem Appendix, stripped all front/back matter and Gutenberg legal boilerplate, merged lone aphorism-number lines into their following paragraph, normalized blank-line paragraph spacing.
headings: A DANCING SONG TO THE MISTRAL WIND.[3]
anomalies_found_and_fixed: Stripped Gutenberg license header/footer, title page, Table of Contents, and the series editor's (Oscar Levy's) EDITORIAL NOTE essay (kept Nietzsche's own Preface to the Second Edition, the 'Jest, Ruse, and Revenge' verse prelude, Books First-Fifth, and the closing poem Appendix).
Merged 449 standalone aphorism-number marker lines (e.g. '1.') into the start of the following paragraph, since in this edition every aphorism number sits alone on its own line.

This 1910 Common/Levy translation is titled 'The Joyful Wisdom ("La Gaya Scienza")' -- the same work commonly sold today as 'The Gay Science'; body text left exactly as translated, only the file/library naming uses the modern title.
BOOK FIRST/SECOND/THIRD/FOURTH/FIFTH and APPENDIX headings recognized as chapter-level headings (all-caps short lines); PREFACE and the verse prelude also recognized as headings.

nearer to the _experiences_
